title: GDScript: outer variables referenced in lambda closures are not updating
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in 4.6.1 stable (14d19694e) ### System information Godot v4.6.1.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon RX 6800 (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.21041.1000) - AMD FX(tm)-6300 Six-Core Processor (6 threads) - 15.90 GiB memory ### Issue description Given a lambda references a variables outside its body, when the lambda is invoked, it doesn't see changes to the variables if they were changed in between the time the lambda was created and invoked. In other words, the lambda function only gets a snapshot of the outer variable's value, so subsequent lambda invocations are only using the initial value it received from the outer variable at the time of its creation. There doesn't seem to be clear documentation on the expected behavior, so this may not be a bug. It does, however, differ in behavior compared to other languages like javascript. There are a few reasons why it'd be useful for closures to use the most up-to-date value of outer variables. A big one (imo) would be having the ability to setup and teardown signal connections. ```GDScript # simplified example, but imagine wanting to disconnect some lambdas from a bunch of signals, after an `ended` signal is emitted var started_callable: Callable = func(): pass var something_happened_callable: Callable = func(): pass var ended_callable: Callable ended_callable = func(): on_ended.call() started.disconnect(started_callable) something_happened.disconnect(something_happened_callable) ended.disconnect(ended_callable) # currently, an error is thrown because `ended_callable` is null started.connect(started_callable) something_happened.connect(something_happened_callable) ended.connect(ended_callable) ``` ### Steps to reproduce GDScript: ```GDScript extends Node2D func _ready() -> void: var x = 1 var fn = func(): print("fn(1): %d" % [x]) x += 1 print("fn(2): %d" % [x]) return x print(x) # expected: 1; actual: 1 print(fn.call()) # expected: 2; actual: 2 print(x) # expected: 2; actual: 1 print("---") x = 10 print(x) # expected: 10; actual: 10 print(fn.call()) # expected: 11; actual: 2 print(x) # expected: 11; actual: 10 ``` Output: Javascript: ```javascript var x = 1 var fn = () => { console.log(`fn(1): ${x}`) x += 1 console.log(`fn(2): ${x}`) return x } console.log(x) // expected: 1; actual: 1 console.log(fn()) // expected: 2; actual: 2 console.log(x) //expected: 2; actual: 2 console.log("---") x = 10 console.log(x) // expected: 10; actual: 10 console.log(fn()) // expected: 11; actual: 11 console.log(x) //expected: 11; actual: 11 ``` Output: ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [broken-closure.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25922346/broken-closure.zip)
